explicit_non_claim: This fixture tests whether the same P/N/X/E/V/S grammar can route materially different asset forms. It does not assert current market state, investment attractiveness, historical alpha, or trading action.

cases.P_asset_example: AI compute adoption, capex and monetization reality
cases.stress_assertion: equity analysis must not define universal Xs for other asset forms

cases.P_asset_example: growth, inflation, fiscal supply and policy reaction reality
cases.stress_assertion: rates research must work without a corporate value-control-point ontology

cases.P_asset_example: supply, demand, inventory, cost curve and capacity reality
cases.stress_assertion: commodity asymmetry must route through scarcity/inventory elasticity rather than issuer moat

cases.P_asset_example: real-rate, fiscal-monetary, reserve-demand and currency-credibility reality
cases.N_example: monetary credibility, reserve diversification and policy-regime expectations
cases.stress_assertion: gold must not be forced into an industrial commodity-only model

cases.P_asset_example: relative growth, policy, rate differential, balance-of-payments and intervention reality
cases.N_example: policy divergence, carry persistence and intervention expectations
cases.stress_assertion: FX asymmetry must route through relative policy/carry/flow rather than absolute single-country fundamentals

pass_conditions: all five cases use the same human P/N/X/E/V/S grammar
A0 asset form differs across cases
A1 pricing archetype can be multi-valued
Xs family differs by asset form/pricing mechanism
R is available as P.capital machine context and is not modeled as a fourth human world
no case emits buy/sell, target price, recommended weight, live sizing or execution
